impact: Demonstrated one-click exfiltration of email content, security codes, meeting details and private organisational files reachable by Microsoft 365 Copilot Enterprise Search. Mitigated server-side by Microsoft; not publicly disclosed or exploited at release per MSRC.
mitigations: Microsoft fully mitigated the vulnerability; no customer action is required (MSRC).

Varonis: monitor for suspicious Copilot Search URLs, review content-security allowlists for domains that fetch user-supplied URLs, and sanitise AI output at render time; users should inspect Microsoft 365 links with long encoded parameters.
name: SearchLeak — one-click data exfiltration via Microsoft 365 Copilot Enterprise Search (CVE-2026-42824)

sources.title: SearchLeak: How We Turned M365 Copilot Into a One-Click Data Exfiltration Weapon
M365 Copilot Information Disclosure Vulnerability (CVE-2026-42824), CSAF advisory

summary: Varonis Threat Labs (researcher Dolev Taler) disclosed SearchLeak, a one-click vulnerability in Microsoft 365 Copilot Enterprise Search. A crafted link caused Copilot to treat attacker-supplied text as a prompt, search the victim's mailbox, calendar and indexed organisational content, and send the results to an attacker-controlled server by chaining output-rendering and content-security weaknesses. Microsoft assigned CVE-2026-42824 (Information Disclosure, CVSS 6.5) on 2026-06-04 and states the issue was fully mitigated server-side with no customer action required.
